fields.reasoning: The measured -parallel 12 ran with 0 failures, but the VM OOM-crashed on 2026-11-14 when parallel suites spawned about 1,600 script children, and the owner has 4 cores and at most 24 GB to give. Once scripts stop sleeping (the scaled clock) they are CPU-bound, so more than twice the cores adds memory and children, not speed; 8 keeps one suite well inside a 6 GB, 300-task scope.
fields.statement: cmd/rhiza's scripts run at -parallel of twice the CPU count, at most 8, unless RHIZA_TEST_SCRIPT_PARALLEL names another positive number; on the 4-core VM that is 8

fields.acceptance: make -n test and make -n test-scripts SHARD=1/4 show -parallel 8 on a 4-core machine and -parallel 3 with RHIZA_TEST_SCRIPT_PARALLEL=3; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run '^TestMakeTestShardTargets$' covers both; failure case: RHIZA_TEST_SCRIPT_PARALLEL=0 or abc falls back to the default rather than passing -parallel 0. Speedup and memory measure (orchestrator, quiet VM): go clean -testcache && systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=6G -p TasksMax=300 -- /usr/bin/time -f '%e s %M KB' go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza passes without hitting either cap, faster than at -parallel 4. Touches Makefile, cmd/rhiza/makeupdate_test.go. Must not raise the cap above 8 or drop the machine-wide test lock.
fields.statement: make test and make test-scripts run cmd/rhiza's scripts at a -parallel of twice the CPU count capped at 8, or RHIZA_TEST_SCRIPT_PARALLEL when it is a positive integer, instead of go test's default of GOMAXPROCS.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./tools/scripttimings turns a go test -json fixture of TestScripts subtests into the sorted name and seconds lines, keeping the previous time for a script that failed or did not run; failure case: input with no passing TestScripts subtest exits non-zero and leaves the file unchanged; the checked-in file has a line for every cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/*.txtar, recorded after the scaled clock landed. Touches tools/scripttimings/, Makefile, cmd/rhiza/testdata/script-timings.tsv. Must not add a module dependency.
fields.statement: cmd/rhiza/testdata/script-timings.tsv, checked in, holds each script's recorded wall time (name, tab, seconds, sorted by name), and make script-timings regenerates it from a go test -json run of TestScripts through a small Go tool under tools/scripttimings.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run '^TestScriptOrder$' shows: given timings, scripts come in descending seconds, ties and scripts missing from the file by name, and every *.txtar exactly once; failure case: a malformed timings line (no tab, or seconds not a number) fails with the file's line number. Touches cmd/rhiza/main_test.go and a new cmd/rhiza/order_test.go. Must not change any script's content or environment.
fields.statement: TestScripts hands testscript its scripts longest first by script-timings.tsv, scripts missing from the file after them by name, so the longest scripts never start last and hold the run's tail.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run '^(TestScriptShard|TestScriptShardEnvError)$' shows the shards disjoint and covering every script, and with the checked-in timings each shard's total within 15% of the mean; failure case: RHIZA_TEST_SHARD=0/4, 5/4 and 1/0 are still refused. The test-scripts-sharded capability's statement says the split is weighted. Measure (orchestrator, after 5 PRs): gh run view <run> --json jobs shows the four scripts jobs within 60 s of each other (2026-11-15: 61-239 s). Touches cmd/rhiza/main_test.go, cmd/rhiza/shard_test.go. Must not change the shard env format or the CI matrix.
fields.statement: RHIZA_TEST_SHARD=i/n splits cmd/rhiza's scripts by recorded time instead of round-robin by name: each script, longest first by script-timings.tsv (a missing one weighted at the median), goes to the shard with the least total so far, so CI's four script shards take about the same time.

set.statement: TestScripts runs one shard of cmd/rhiza's scripts when RHIZA_TEST_SHARD=i/n is set (1-based): the scripts assigned to shard i when each, longest first by cmd/rhiza/testdata/script-timings.tsv, goes to the shard with the least recorded time so far, passed as testscript Files; unset, it runs every script, longest first (@{01M7EQE69J35XJW25SPBZBH1MS}).
